# BPCS Interlock Record: Template and Worked Example

## 1. How the template meets your three goals

| Goal | Mechanism |
|---|---|
| Configurer can implement | Sections 3-7 state the cause, effect, latch, reset, bypass, and fail behavior. They contain no implementation detail (no blocks or routines). |
| FAT team can write a test step | Each requirement (FR-) has one test method. Section 10 gives one FAT step per requirement. |
| No copied setpoints | Every number lives in the project setpoint register, keyed by SP-ID. This record, the alarm database, the HMI, and the FAT sheets cite the SP-ID only. If a value changes, change the register row and nothing else. |

Rules for authors:
- Write no numeric value in prose, tables, or FAT steps. Cite the SP-ID.
- Give each requirement the ID `FR-<unit>-NNN` and a test method. Rewrite or remove any requirement you cannot test.
- Keep SIS functions out. Reference the SRS ID only (field 1.5).
- Keep one record per interlock. Assign IDs as `IL-<unit>-NNN`.

---

## 3. Worked example: IL-H1100-001, Low fuel gas pressure to heater H-1100

I assumed the unit is heater H-1100 and that the tags marked "assumed" exist. Confirm both against the instrument index.

### 1. Header
| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| 1.1 | IL-H1100-001, Low fuel gas pressure closes main fuel valve |
| 1.2 | Heater H-1100, fuel gas supply module |
| 1.3 | Rev A, Draft for operations review, 2026-10-18 |
| 1.4 | Legacy printout and C&E drawing references: TBD (see open item OI-6) |
| 1.5 | SIS cross-reference: none known. See OI-1. |
| 1.6 | Prevents flame instability from low burner pressure. The interlock gives no SIL credit. It acts before any SIS low-low function. |

### 2. Tags
| Tag | Role | Signal | Fail position or state |
|---|---|---|---|
| PT-1105 | Cause: fuel gas header pressure, upstream of XV-1106 | 4-20 mA, hardwired | Low signal reads as bad PV |
| XV-1106 | Effect: main fuel gas shutoff valve | Discrete, solenoid XY-1106 | Fails closed. XY-1106 de-energizes to close. |
| ZSC-1106 (assumed) | Feedback: valve closed | Discrete | Not closed after the timeout in SP list means fail-to-close |
| ZSO-1106 (assumed) | Feedback: valve open | Discrete | |
| HS-1106 (assumed) | Operator open command, faceplate | DCS command | |
| HS-1105 (assumed) | Interlock reset command, faceplate | DCS command | |
| HS-1107 (assumed) | Maintenance bypass command for PT-1105 | DCS command | |

### 3. States and transitions
| State | Entry condition | Allowed exits | Initiator |
|---|---|---|---|
| NORMAL | PT-1105 above the reset value, no trip latched | To TRIPPED. To BYPASSED. | Auto. Operator for bypass. |
| TRIPPED (latched) | Trip condition true for the trip delay, or bad PV, or power-up | To RESET-READY | Auto |
| RESET-READY | PT-1105 above the reset value, PV good, XV-1106 confirmed closed | To NORMAL on reset. To TRIPPED if the trip condition returns. | Operator (HS-1105) |
| BYPASSED | Operator sets HS-1107 with the bypass reason entered | To NORMAL on cancel or on bypass timer expiry | Operator. Timer is automatic. |

Automation level: trip is automatic. Reset and valve re-open are manual. The heater restart sequence is outside this record (see the H-1100 heater narrative).

### 4. Cause-and-effect rows
| Cause | Effect | Latched / auto-reset | Reset method |
|---|---|---|---|
| PT-1105 below trip setpoint for trip delay | De-energize XY-1106, which closes XV-1106 | Latched | Operator pushes HS-1105 when in RESET-READY. Operator then opens XV-1106 with HS-1106. |
| PT-1105 bad PV | Same as above | Latched | Same as above, after PV is good |
| Controller power-up or restart | Same as above | Latched | Same as above |

### 5. Trip logic definition
| Item | Entry |
|---|---|
| 5.1 | Trip when PT-1105 is below SP-H1100-001. |
| 5.2 | Single transmitter. A bad PV counts as a trip. |
| 5.3 | Trip delay is SP-H1100-003. |
| 5.4 | Reset needs PT-1105 above SP-H1100-002, PV good, ZSC-1106 closed, and an operator push of HS-1105. |
| 5.5 | The operator may bypass for PT-1105 maintenance only. The bypass ends at SP-H1100-006. Bypass alarm is XA-1107. Bypass is blocked when PV is good and below SP-H1100-001 (it cannot mask an active trip). |
| 5.6 | After a trip, XV-1106 stays closed until the operator opens it. No auto-reopen. |

### 6. Abnormal handling
| Condition | Interlock response | Output state |
|---|---|---|
| PT-1105 signal below SP-H1100-004 or above SP-H1100-005 | Bad PV. Trip and latch. Raise XA-1108. | XV-1106 closed |
| Loss of the I/O module that carries PT-1105 or XY-1106 | Treat as bad PV. Trip and latch. | XV-1106 closed |
| Loss of link between controller and operator station | Logic continues. Operator cannot reset or bypass until the link returns. | No change |
| Power loss to XY-1106 | Valve closes by spring | XV-1106 closed |
| Controller power loss and restart | Start in TRIPPED. Needs a manual reset. | XV-1106 closed |
| XV-1106 not closed within SP-H1100-007 after trip | Raise XA-1106. Operator closes the manual block valve per the operating procedure. | Per alarm response |

### 7. Alarms (provisional; move to the alarm database when it exists)
| Tag | Condition | Priority | Operator response |
|---|---|---|---|
| PAL-1105 | PT-1105 below SP-H1100-008 | Medium | Check fuel gas supply. Raise pressure before the trip. |
| XA-1105 | Interlock TRIPPED | High | Check the heater state. Find the cause. Do not reset until the cause is clear. |
| XA-1106 | XV-1106 not closed after trip | High | Close the manual block valve. Tell the shift supervisor. |
| XA-1107 | Bypass active | Medium | Make sure maintenance is in progress. Cancel the bypass at job end. |
| XA-1108 | PT-1105 bad PV | High | Call instrument maintenance. |

### 8. Operator interface
- The H-1100 fuel gas display shows PT-1105, the interlock state, and the XV-1106 position.
- The operator can push HS-1105 (reset) only in RESET-READY. The display greys out the button in other states.
- The operator can set the bypass only after entering a reason. The display shows the remaining bypass time.
- On RESET-READY, the display prompts: "Fuel gas pressure is restored. Reset the interlock, then open XV-1106."
- Operations must sign off these states and prompts (see section 13).

### 9. Requirements
| ID | Requirement | Test method |
|---|---|---|
| FR-H1100-001 | Close XV-1106 when PT-1105 stays below SP-H1100-001 for SP-H1100-003. | FAT step 2 |
| FR-H1100-002 | Do not trip when PT-1105 stays below SP-H1100-001 for less than SP-H1100-003. | FAT step 3 |
| FR-H1100-003 | Latch the trip. Do not auto-reset when PT-1105 recovers. | FAT step 4 |
| FR-H1100-004 | Allow reset only when PT-1105 is above SP-H1100-002, PV is good, and ZSC-1106 shows closed. | FAT steps 5, 6 |
| FR-H1100-005 | Do not reopen XV-1106 on reset. Require an operator open command. | FAT step 7 |
| FR-H1100-006 | Trip and latch on bad PV when the PT-1105 signal passes SP-H1100-004 or SP-H1100-005. | FAT step 8 |
| FR-H1100-007 | Start in TRIPPED after controller restart. | FAT step 9 |
| FR-H1100-008 | Close XV-1106 when XY-1106 loses power. | FAT step 10 (SAT also) |
| FR-H1100-009 | Raise XA-1106 when ZSC-1106 is not closed within SP-H1100-007 after trip. | FAT step 11 |
| FR-H1100-010 | Allow bypass only with a reason entered. End the bypass at SP-H1100-006. Block bypass during an active trip. | FAT steps 12, 13 |
| FR-H1100-011 | Raise PAL-1105 when PT-1105 is below SP-H1100-008. | FAT step 1 |
| FR-H1100-012 | Keep trip logic running when the operator-station link is lost. | FAT step 14 |

### 10. FAT steps
Use the SP-ID values from the register. Simulate PT-1105 with a loop calibrator.

| Step | Req | Action | Expected result | P/F |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 011 | Set PT-1105 below SP-H1100-008 and above SP-H1100-001. | PAL-1105 active. XV-1106 stays open. | |
| 2 | 001 | Set PT-1105 below SP-H1100-001. Hold for SP-H1100-003. | XY-1106 de-energizes. XV-1106 closes. XA-1105 active. State is TRIPPED. | |
| 3 | 002 | Reset the test. Set PT-1105 below SP-H1100-001 for less than SP-H1100-003, then restore. | No trip. | |
| 4 | 003 | After step 2, set PT-1105 above SP-H1100-002. | State stays TRIPPED. XV-1106 stays closed. | |
| 5 | 004 | With PT-1105 between SP-H1100-001 and SP-H1100-002, push HS-1105. | Reset refused. | |
| 6 | 004 | With PT-1105 above SP-H1100-002, force ZSC-1106 not closed. Push HS-1105. | Reset refused. Then restore ZSC-1106 and repeat. Reset accepted. | |
| 7 | 005 | After reset, check XV-1106. Push HS-1106. | XV-1106 stays closed after reset. XV-1106 opens only after HS-1106. | |
| 8 | 006 | Set PT-1105 current past SP-H1100-004, then past SP-H1100-005. | Trip and latch each time. XA-1108 active. | |
| 9 | 007 | Restart the controller with PT-1105 healthy. | State is TRIPPED. XV-1106 closed. | |
| 10 | 008 | Remove power from XY-1106. | XV-1106 closes. | |
| 11 | 009 | Trip, then hold ZSC-1106 not closed for SP-H1100-007. | XA-1106 active. | |
| 12 | 010 | Set bypass with no reason. Then set bypass with a reason. | First refused. Second accepted. XA-1107 active. Timer visible. | |
| 13 | 010 | Hold bypass until SP-H1100-006. Then try bypass during an active trip. | Bypass ends at the limit. Bypass during a trip is refused. | |
| 14 | 012 | Disconnect the operator-station link. Trip PT-1105. | XV-1106 closes. No logic fault. | |

### 11. Setpoint register extract
All values are provisional. Operations and process must confirm each one against the heater design basis and the burner vendor data.

| ID | Description | Value | Units | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| SP-H1100-001 | Low pressure trip (PT-1105) | 12.0 | psig | confirm |
| SP-H1100-002 | Reset permissive (PT-1105) | 15.0 | psig | confirm |
| SP-H1100-003 | Trip delay | 2 | s | confirm |
| SP-H1100-004 | Bad PV, signal low | 3.6 | mA | confirm |
| SP-H1100-005 | Bad PV, signal high | 21.0 | mA | confirm |
| SP-H1100-006 | Maximum bypass time | 8 | h | confirm |
| SP-H1100-007 | XV-1106 close-confirm timeout | 10 | s | confirm |
| SP-H1100-008 | Low pressure pre-alarm (PAL-1105) | 18.0 | psig | confirm |

### 12. Open items
| # | Item | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| OI-1 | Confirm that no SIS function uses PT-1105 or XV-1106. If one does, move that function to the SRS and add the cross-reference in 1.5. Confirm PT-1105 is independent of any SIS transmitter. | Process safety engineer | 2026-11-13 |
| OI-2 | Confirm all values in the setpoint register (the trip value must stay above any SIS low-low value). | Process engineer | 2026-11-13 |
| OI-3 | Confirm the PT-1105 location is upstream of XV-1106, so pressure is readable when the valve is closed. | Process engineer | 2026-11-06 |
| OI-4 | Confirm the tags marked "assumed" (ZSC/ZSO-1106, HS-1105/1106/1107, XA-1105 to XA-1108) against the instrument index. | Controls lead | 2026-11-06 |
| OI-5 | Move alarms to the rationalized alarm database and set final priorities. | Controls lead and operations | 2026-11-27 |
| OI-6 | Attach the legacy printout and C&E drawing references to 1.4. | Migration engineer | 2026-11-06 |
| OI-7 | Operations sign-off on states, prompts, and the bypass rule. | Operations supervisor | 2026-11-27 |

### 13. Sign-off and change log

| Process | | |

## 4. Suggested practices for 40 units

1. **One register for all setpoints.** Key it by `SP-<unit>-NNN`. Have the configurer load values from it. Have the alarm database and FAT sheets cite the SP-ID only.
2. **Check the SIS boundary first.** For each legacy interlock, decide BPCS or SIS before you write the record. Put every SIS function in the SRS and reference it in field 1.5.
3. **Review legacy logic against the new record.** For each migrated interlock, compare the old trip direction, delay, latch, and fail position with the new record. Log every difference. Legacy printouts often hold undocumented behavior, such as hidden delays or auto-reset.
4. **Generate FAT sheets from section 9 and 10.** One requirement gives one FAT step, so a missing test shows up as a gap in the table.
5. **Use MOC after construction starts.** Add revision clouds and a change-log entry for each change.

If you share the instrument index format or your alarm philosophy, I can align the tag naming and alarm priorities. I can also convert the template to a spreadsheet layout with one row per requirement.
